question: The price of fuel decreases by 45%, 15% and 50% in three successive months, but increases by 70% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price? (Rounded off to two decimal places)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net factor = (1 − 0.45)(1 − 0.15)(1 − 0.50)(1 + 0.70)

= 0.55 × 0.85 × 0.50 × 1.70

= 0.397375

% change = (0.397375 − 1) × 100

= −60.2625%

**∴ Answer = 60.26% decrease**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Decrease = 45%, 15%, 50%

Increase = 70%

**Formula used:**

Successive percentage change ⇒ multiply factors

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let original price = 100

⇒ After 1st decrease ⇒ 100 × 0.55 = 55

⇒ After 2nd decrease ⇒ 55 × 0.85 = 46.75

⇒ After 3rd decrease ⇒ 46.75 × 0.50 = 23.375

⇒ After 4th increase ⇒ 23.375 × 1.70 = 39.7375

⇒ Final price = 39.7375

⇒ Change = 39.7375 − 100 = −60.2625

⇒ % change = −60.26%

**∴ The correct answer is 60.26% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Change

Multiply all increase/decrease factors

Key Rule

Final value = Initial × product of factors

Shortcut

Use decimal form of percentages
